role.altitude: The social work teacher keeps lecturing, meeting supervisees, visiting placements, assessing papers, deciding grades and reshaping courses with colleagues; checking citation formats, writing the same feedback, coordinating placements by mail and compiling evaluation exports shrink.
skills_to_grow: Editing drafted feedback so it stays the teacher's own
role.ambitious_version: A teacher whose marking time goes to the arguments in the papers, not to formatting.

tasks.short: Update lecture content with recent research, prepare slides and examples, plan the session, deliver lectures on topics such as family behavior or child and adolescent mental health, answer follow-up questions, upload materials and meet students afterwards.

steps.what: Teacher updates lecture content with recent research

loop.input: The lecture topic and an abstract and citation database.
loop.output: Recent papers and topic summaries, each linked to its source.
loop.check: The teacher opens every cited paper before using it in a lecture.
loop.stop: The teacher searches by hand when known key papers are missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Findings are spread over social work, psychology and policy journals.

steps.what: Teacher prepares lecture slides and case examples

loop.input: The teacher's outline, learning outcomes and checked sources.
loop.output: Draft slides and fictional case examples.
loop.check: The teacher reads every slide; every fact must cite a checked source; cases must be fictional.
loop.stop: The teacher writes slides by hand when two drafts miss the point.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each lecture argues its own line.

steps.what: Teacher plans the session flow and activities
Teacher delivers lectures to undergraduate or graduate students
Teacher answers the same follow-up questions from several students by mail
Teacher uploads slides to the learning environment
Teacher talks with students after the lecture

tasks.design: A literature tool returns recent papers and topic summaries with links, and the teacher opens each source. A drafting step turns the teacher's outline and checked sources into draft slides and fictional case examples, and the teacher reads every slide. No client data enters any tool. A course question forum in the learning environment lets one answer reach every student who asks the same thing. Planning, lecturing and talking with students stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lectures were updated by hand searches and slides built from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Literature tools with links, drafting from the teacher's outline and course forums.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive topics where examples must be handled with care.
tasks.human_edge: Bringing practice experience into the room.

evidence.claim: A literature database tool gives topic summaries and foundational papers.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing and delivering lectures; preparing syllabi and handouts (task 6244) and moderating discussions (task 6238) are sibling tasks.
s5 saves answering the same question several times.
Planning, lecturing and talking with students keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of lectures revised each year.
research_questions: Is preparation time shorter without weaker lectures?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: established lectures; high: new or heavily revised lectures.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet supervisees, comment on drafts, coordinate internship placements, track progress, visit placements, complete evaluations and answer questions to supervise undergraduate or graduate teaching, internship and research work.

steps.what: Teacher meets supervisees to discuss teaching, internship and research work
Teacher reads drafts and writes comments, including on citation and structure
Teacher coordinates internship placements with agencies and students by mail
Teacher tracks supervisees' milestones and deadlines in a spreadsheet
Teacher visits internship sites
Teacher copies the field supervisor's assessment into the university evaluation form
Teacher answers supervisee questions by mail

tasks.design: An internship portal holds each placement's learning agreement, hours, milestones and the field supervisor's assessment. Student, agency and teacher work in one record instead of three-way mail, and the teacher no longer copies the assessment into a separate form. A milestone view replaces the tracking spreadsheet. Formal feedback on citation style and structure comes from a feedback tool whose criteria the teacher sets, and the teacher's comments focus on content. Meeting supervisees, site visits and judgements on the work stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Placements ran on three-way mail and assessments were copied between forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Internship portals and criteria-based feedback tools.
tasks.still_hard: Agencies that will not use the portal.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a student is overwhelmed by a difficult placement.
tasks.altitude: Less mail and copying; supervision stays.

evidence.claim: A feedback tool gives formative feedback on writing criteria such as citation style; teachers edit the criteria.

assumptions: Boundary: supervising teaching, internship and research work; supervising lab and field work (task 6243) and advising on careers (task 6250) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s3 and s6: about 60% of agencies use the internship portal; s3 and s6 are priced at that share.
s6 saves copying the field supervisor's assessment; the teacher still decides the result.
Meetings, visits and answers keep their full time.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few agencies on the portal; high: most placements in the portal.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check formal requirements, read and evaluate students' class work, assignments and papers against the rubric, write feedback, decide the grade, enter it, copy it to the records system, answer questions and discuss borderline cases.

steps.what: Teacher checks length, citation style and references of each paper
Teacher reads and evaluates each paper against the rubric
Teacher writes feedback comments per rubric item

loop.input: The teacher's rubric marks and short notes per paper.
loop.output: Draft feedback text per rubric item.
loop.check: Each comment must quote a passage from the paper and follow the teacher's mark; the teacher edits every comment. No score is suggested.
loop.stop: The teacher writes the feedback when a rubric item lacks a quoted passage.
loop.why_not_simpler: Feedback must speak to each student's text.

steps.what: Teacher decides the grade
Teacher enters grades and feedback in the learning environment
Teacher copies grades from the learning environment into the student information system
Teacher answers students' questions about their grades
Teacher discusses borderline papers with a second marker

tasks.design: Code checks each submission for length, citation format and whether references resolve, instead of the teacher checking by hand. A drafting step turns the teacher's rubric marks and short notes into feedback text. Each comment quotes a passage and the teacher edits every one, and no score is suggested. Reading, evaluating, deciding grades, second marking and answering students stay with the teacher, who is the appointed examiner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Formal checks and feedback text were done by hand for every paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Automated formal checks and feedback drafted from the teacher's notes.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising real reflection on a hard case.
tasks.altitude: Less checking and typing; judgement stays.

evidence.claim: A learning platform feature drafts text and rubric feedback from instructor notes.
In a randomised trial with 1,366 essays, assistants agreed with 88% of AI feedback judgements and student revisions improved; no time data.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk from 2 December 2027, so the tool here suggests no scores.

assumptions: Boundary: evaluating and grading class work and papers; compiling and grading examinations (task 6249) and maintaining grade records (task 6251) are sibling tasks.
s6 is part of maintaining grade records, which sibling task 6251 covers; its saving is counted there.
s3 is priced at 70 because the teacher edits every comment.
Reading, deciding, second marking and answering keep their full time.
research_questions: Is feedback returned sooner with the same quality?

incremental.description: Teacher keeps rubric criteria and checks current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short reflective work; high: long papers with many references.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile course evaluations and results, read student comments, map outcomes to competences, discuss changes with colleagues, revise course content and methods, submit changes and observe teaching to plan, evaluate and revise curricula.

steps.what: Teacher compiles course evaluation scores and pass rates in a spreadsheet
Teacher reads student comments from course evaluations

loop.input: Anonymous student comments from the course evaluation.
loop.output: Comments grouped by theme, each with its quotes.
loop.check: The teacher reads the quotes in every theme; a sample of groupings is checked against the raw comments.
loop.stop: The teacher reads all comments when groupings disagree with the sample.

steps.what: Teacher maps course outcomes to programme outcomes and professional competences in a matrix
Teacher discusses curricula changes with colleagues and the programme committee
Teacher revises course content, materials and methods of instruction
Teacher mails course changes to the curriculum committee
Teacher observes a colleague's class or is observed

tasks.design: A course dashboard shows evaluation scores and pass rates per course and year, instead of exports compiled in a spreadsheet. A grouping step sorts anonymous comments by theme with their quotes, and the teacher reads every theme. A curriculum map tool links course outcomes to programme outcomes and professional competences and shows gaps, instead of a matrix kept by hand. Course changes go through the course catalogue's change form instead of mail. Discussing, revising and observing teaching stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evaluation data and outcome matrices were compiled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Course dashboards, comment grouping and curriculum map tools.
tasks.still_hard: Competence frameworks that change every few years.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which change a programme committee will accept.

evidence.claim: Records, dashboards and change forms replace spreadsheets and mail for course administration.

assumptions: Boundary: planning and revising curricula; preparing syllabi and handouts (task 6244) and collaborating with agencies (task 6248) are sibling tasks.
s1 and s3 save compiling exports and keeping a matrix by hand; s6 saves mailing changes.
Evaluation comments are anonymous before grouping.
Discussing, revising and observing keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of courses revised per year.

incremental.description: Teacher keeps the curriculum map current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: stable courses; high: programmes under review.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
